newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers to debate long-distance calls.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to debate long-distance calls.

text.p: European Union telecommunications ministers will debate on Friday how consumers should make long-distance and international calls in an era of free competition between phone companies.
The European Commission has proposed that governments introduce a system known as "carrier pre-selection" by January 1, 2000.
That would ensure that consumers can make long-distance calls without dialing a special code -- no matter which phone company they choose to handle those calls.

The proposal, which will be discussed by ministers in Luxembourg, aims to break the grip of the traditional phone monopolies as part of the EU's effort to open most of its telecoms markets to competition by January 1, 1998.
However, Britain opposes the move and has persuaded some other EU states that it needs more study, diplomats said.
Britain is concerned because its cable TV companies are investing heavily in networks that provide local phone service, offering tough competition to British Telecom, they said.
Carrier pre-selection would make it easier for consumers to bypass them for lucrative long-distance calls and could discourage newcomers from investing in "local loops", Britain argues.
But other countries, including France and Germany, say that carrier pre-selection is essential to promoting competition.
The ministers will try to adopt a statement on the issue, but it is up to the Commission to decide what legislation to propose.
The ministers will also address the question of number "portability" -- the ability of consumers to take their numbers with them when they change phone companies.

The Commission wants governments to introduce portability by January 1, 2000. While all countries agree that the practice is important, they differ on how quickly to bring it in, diplomats said. -- Suzanne Perry, Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
